title: "Pay Start cutover packet"
description: "Source and operator checklist for a future Pay Worker cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers

Pay has a TanStack Start/Void candidate. Production publication and routing are
held; this packet records the source target and checks required before Rex
authorizes a cutover. It does not authorize deployment, payment activity,
provider changes or data writes.

## Worker and configuration

- Worker: `tuturuuu-pay` for production; the staging Worker name for the
  isolated staging candidate.
- Hosts: `pay.tuturuuu.com` and the `/pay` mount on `tuturuuu.com`. Staging
  must use the separately approved staging host and zone.
- Build: `cd apps/pay && bun run build:cloudflare`.
- Static asset binding: `ASSETS`. Optional internal API origin variable:
  `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`.
- Staging profile variable names: `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`,
  `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL`,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `PAY_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, and
  `POLAR_SANDBOX`. Supply sandbox-only provider values through the approved
  environment; never put credentials in this page or profile.
- Runtime secret names: `CRON_SECRET`, `POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN`,
  `POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, and
  `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`. Configure them only through the protected
  runtime secret store. This packet contains names, never values.

## Smoke checks

After an authorized cutover, run the public build identity probes against both
hosts and verify the native runtime header and expected source SHA:

```sh
curl -fsS -D - https://pay.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
curl -fsSI https://tuturuuu.com/pay/api/build-info
```

The release operator must also run the signed-in billing and sandbox checkout
smokes in [Pay staging acceptance](./pay-start), including webhook signature
rejection, then watch authentication and 5xx behavior. Do not invoke billing,
webhook, cron or migration endpoints as a smoke substitute.

## Rollback

Before routing changes, Rex records the immutable Vercel deployment ID and the
exact routes, custom domains and DNS records being replaced, plus the one-step
restore command and rollback owner. No deployment ID is recorded in this
repository, so Rex must capture it. Restore that routing to the prior deployment
immediately if smoke or the post-cutover watch regresses. Keep the deployment
available for the full release cycle.

## Credential-free local verification

Pay has two build paths: retained Next.js (`next.config.ts`, `vercel.json`) and
native TanStack Start with Vite+, Void and the shared Start bridge. Use the native
path for Worker acceptance; adding OpenNext creates a second adapter to maintain.
Vercel Deployment Protection is a hosting-level gate in front of pages, API
responses and static assets. It is not Pay session authentication. The source
cannot establish the live Vercel project's protection settings; owner readback
must capture the protected deployment and observed challenge. No bypass token or
application-auth exception is required for loopback Worker smoke.

The staging profile remains root-only on its exact staging host and keeps
Cloudflare Access and sandbox isolation. The production profile builds assets
under `/pay/`, admits `tuturuuu.com/pay` and the legacy root host, and selects
`TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_PAY=on` with `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_PAY_REDIRECT_STATUS=301`. Its
`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and `PAY_APP_URL` have the canonical `/pay` suffix with no
trailing slash. Browser GET/HEAD navigations on the legacy host preserve the
path/query in a 301; `/pay/` canonicalizes to `/pay`. APIs, assets, server functions
and non-navigation requests are not redirected. Provider deliveries must never
rely on a browser redirect preserving a POST body.

Run commands from the repository root, using the pinned Bun version. Local
builds require an explicitly authorized build host; ordinary validation uses CI.
No command below deploys or authenticates to a provider:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
ttr resources run -- bun turbo run build --filter='@tuturuuu/pay^...' --concurrency=1
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/pay test --maxWorkers=2
python3 scripts/ci/pay-native-artifact.test.py
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/pay type-check:cloudflare
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/pay build:cloudflare
```

The default build is staging. Select `VITE_PAY_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` for a
separate production candidate; do not reuse staging output. `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH`
is checked against the profile at build time. Keep all real provider credentials
out of the build and smoke environment. Owner-supplied public build settings are
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`; runtime
secret names are listed above. Optional `PLATFORM_LOG_DRAIN_DATABASE_URL`,
`PLATFORM_LOG_DRAIN_ENABLED`, and `PLATFORM_LOG_DRAIN_PROJECT_ID` control the
existing log drain. Never print or store their values in receipts.

The plain-JavaScript local harness requires an emitted artifact and runs on Node
22 without a TypeScript loader:

```sh
cd apps/pay
WRANGLER_LOG=error node --test cloudflare/local-worker-smoke.mjs
# After a separate production-profile build:
VITE_PAY_NATIVE_PROFILE=production WRANGLER_LOG=error node --test cloudflare/local-worker-smoke.mjs
```

Wrangler rewrites same-host redirect schemes to its local listener protocol;
source policy tests require the HTTPS production target. CI retains the generated
`native-built-worker.runtime.mjs` acceptance suite with its build identity channel.

The harness copies output to disposable storage, binds loopback only, forbids
provider auth and denies outbound requests. A passing source test or staging
artifact does not establish production mount hydration. Before cutover, seal and
exercise a production-profile artifact at the apex with the same egress fence;
require exact-commit CI, independent security review and hosted sandbox acceptance.

The local harness uses a disposable signing secret and a synthetic
`customer.created` event with no Pay business callback to exercise the actual
webhook route; it requires acceptance before rejecting unsigned/tampered bodies
on both production paths. This does not establish payment side effects or deduplication.
It checks every emitted JS/CSS/font file, MIME types and the RSC
manifest asset URL prefixes, plus public `robots.txt`, root/build identity, mount
neighbours and host rejection. It does not drive signed-in browser hydration.
Browser asset smoke must additionally check generated module imports, font URLs, public
`robots.txt`, favicon/manifest if emitted, lazy chunks, the base head script,
client navigation, server-function requests and app-owned API URLs under `/pay`.
Require correct MIME types, no HTML fallback for missing files, no requests to
apex `/assets` or `/pay/pay`, no external provider traffic, and security headers.
Repeat with a raw Host header: unknown hosts and `/pay-extra` must reject.
The apex gateway must route bare `/pay` (including query strings) as well as
`/pay/*`; a wildcard route alone is insufficient. Rex owns those route/DNS changes.

## Security review gate (D87)

- **Auth:** no proxy/session/MFA/permission or API guard changes. Production gains
  apex route admission; unknown hosts still fail closed. Mounted session mint and
  refresh endpoints remain refused by the shared bridge.
- **Cookies:** no cookie-name/domain/SameSite/Secure changes. Production retains
  the shared root session; staging remains host-only. The bridge strips mounted
  app session writes. Review signed-in billing and central logout before release.
- **CSRF:** no exemptions or bypass added. Mounted cookie mutations enforce the
  shared same-origin check before dispatch. Cookie-less provider deliveries still
  authenticate via their signature handler.
- **Webhooks:** POST `/pay/api/payment/webhooks` strips `/pay` once and dispatches
  the existing Polar `Webhooks` handler. It reads raw `request.text()` and verifies
  `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` with
  `POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` before callbacks. The signature implementation, payload,
  replay policy and business callbacks are unchanged. Both legacy and mounted
  paths retain invalid/missing-signature rejection; the synthetic signed fixture
  verifies raw bytes and rejects tampering/stale timestamps; no redirect or parse/reencode
  is added. Valid signed delivery, timestamp rejection, replay/idempotency and
  provider retry behavior remain mandatory sandbox evidence before switching the
  registered endpoint. Keep legacy delivery routing available through rollback.
- **CORS/CSP/headers:** no CORS permission changes. Existing nonce CSP, noindex,
  no-store and framing policy remain. Asset and WebGL path classification strips
  the mounted prefix so existing cache/sandbox rules apply at the apex too.
- **Operations:** no cron, queue, database migration, payment-provider setting,
  deployment or DNS mutation. The Vercel cron declaration is retained; Rex must
  select one scheduler and prevent duplicate execution at cutover.

Source regression coverage is `cloudflare/mounted-routing.test.ts`, existing Pay
proxy/response tests, and `scripts/ci/pay-native-artifact.test.py`. Independent
security review and real signed sandbox deliveries are release gates, not claims
made by these local tests. Production publication remains held in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`.
